subject: Geo affinity & latency qualification — Storix / Redwood follow-up
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@storix.com>, Elena Park <elena.park@storix.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Geo affinity & latency qualification — Storix / Redwood follow-up

Hi Carlos / Elena,

Thanks again for the call today — good alignment on use case and volume. I wanted to capture the performance/region items we discussed and list concrete next steps so we can scope the pilot: 

Recap of requirements you called out
- Latency target: ≤ 120ms p95 for US-based traffic; ≤ 140ms p95 for EU. APAC is best-effort, target p95 ~200ms.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state 150 concurrent requests, spikes to 700 rps for short bursts (5-10m).
- Average prompt scope: 1.2k tokens (inputs + expected output ~1.6k tokens).
- Streaming: yes, streaming responses for our chat flows is required (chunked outputs).
- Data residency: EU customers must keep request/response data in EU datacenter; logs/audits must be retained in-region.
- Fallback policy: want automatic failover for US<->EU routing but cannot route EU-origin traffic to US for compliance. APAC may route to nearest region or to US if APAC capacity not available.
- Caching: prefix caching would help — approximate reuse of prompts ~18% on average.

Attachments I pushed to this thread: quant_latency_matrix.xlsx (initial perf matrix) and network-diagram-storix.pdf (high-level ingress/egress).

Immediate asks from our side to run a focused qualification: 
1) Confirm a 2-hour perf window next week (preferred: Tue 6/22 09:00-11:00 PT) for peak concurrency run.
2) Share sample payloads (5 representative conversations) and an anonymized EU customer CID for residency validation.
3) Confirm whether Storix will allow outbound egress to Redwood IP block(s) we will share, or whether you need us to come through marketplace/VPC peering.

Proposed Redwood approach (high-level)
- Provision dedicated capacity in US + EU for the pilot (to guarantee residency and predictable latency).
- Enable streaming and continuous batching tuned for 1.2k token prompts (start batch size 4, adapt based on latency windows).
- KV/prefix cache enabled with TTL 10m for chat session reuse.

Next steps
- If the timeslot above works, I will send a perf run checklist and firewall IPs.
- If you prefer, we can scope an EU-only pilot first to validate residency, then add US failover for non-EU traffic.

Thanks — I will loop Laura and Rishi on the ops details.

Best,
Dylan
Dylan Brooks | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
attachments: quant_latency_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), network-diagram-storix.pdf (pdf)

From: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@storix.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@storix.com>
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo affinity & latency qualification — Storix / Redwood follow-up

Thanks Dylan — this is great, and aligns with what we need. Quick answers inline: 

- Latency: 120ms p95 US / 140ms p95 EU is our bar for public-facing features. Internal tools can be laxer.
- Concurrency / spikes: steady 150 concurrent (sustained), we can see sudden ramping to ~700 rps as noted for launches. We can throttle if needed but want a plan to absorb short bursts.
- Tokens: average ~1.2k as you wrote; some long-form prompts up to 3k tokens but rare (<2%).
- Streaming: required for our chat widget, we need chunked events to show partial answers.
- Data residency: EU-origin traffic must remain in EU at all times — cannot be routed through US for inference or logs.

On the asks:
1) 6/22 09:00-11:00 PT works for us.
2) I will drop 5 sample conversations and one anonymized EU CID to this thread by EOD today.
3) We prefer VPC peering for the EU pilot (internal policy). Please share the peering steps and any marketplace options.

Couple of clarifying questions: 
- For APAC, if you don't have region presence, do you recommend routing APAC to US or holding to keep everything in-region (we likely will take higher latency for APAC at first)?
- Can Redwood guarantee that logs/trace data generated during the run will be captured only in-region for EU traffic? What level of audit evidence can you provide?

Appreciate the clear plan — Elena and I will coordinate the sample payloads.

—Carlos
Carlos Mendez | Director of Product Infrastructure | Storix

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: internal@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 11:38:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Geo affinity & latency qualification — Storix / Redwood follow-up

Laura / Rishi — forwarding Storix thread. Key constraints: EU residency strict (no cross-border inference/logging), steady 150 concurrency with 700 rps spikes, streaming required. They prefer VPC peering for EU.

Proposed internal plan (concise):
- Pilot topology: Dedicated EU pool (g4dn/g5 equivalent) behind VPC peering for Storix EU tenants; Dedicated US pool for US traffic. APAC: recommend routing to US for now but honor APAC flag (higher p95 acceptable).
- Routing: geo-affinity at request edge (region based on client IP / app-config). EU-origin requests pinned to EU pool; if EU pool is saturated, auto-scale or degrade by returning 429 / or queue — do NOT failover to US because of compliance. US and APAC may failover between US zones.
- Batching & streaming: start with continuous batching enabled, target batch_size=4, max_latency=40ms. Maintain streaming pipeline to front-end; ensure chunked flush every ~150 tokens.
- Cache: prefix cache enabled, TTL 10m, warm cache for common system prompts.
- Metrics & evidence: capture region-tagged audit logs (request_id, region, timestamp) and provide a time-limited audit bundle post-run. SOC2/HIPAA evidence: handoff to security for tenant isolation attestation.

Action items for us before 6/22 perf window:
1) Rishi: produce firewall / peering IP list + peering steps (doc + quick checklist).
2) Laura: prepare dedicated EU capacity estimate and cost delta for pilot (hourly + burst buffer).
3) I: create perf run plan + test harness and sample load scripts; coordinate test times.

If we decide EU dedicated is heavy, alternative is a Private deployment in EU for them (longer lead time) — mention as optional fallback in the proposal.

Thoughts? I'll draft the customer-facing note once you confirm the peering and capacity numbers.

—Dylan

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Mendez <c.mendez@storix.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Park <elena.park@storix.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Geo affinity & latency qualification — Storix / Redwood follow-up

Hi Carlos / Elena — looping back with concrete next steps and what to expect in the pilot. Thanks again for the quick replies and for sharing sample payloads (received).

What we will deliver for the pilot (summary)
- Provisioned dedicated pools: EU (reserved for EU-origin requests) and US (reserved for US-origin). Pools will be sized to meet your steady concurrency with a burst buffer to absorb the 700rps short spikes.
- Streaming enabled with chunked flush; we will tune to meet p95 targets during the run.
- Data residency guarantee for EU traffic: inference, logs, and trace exports will remain in-region for the duration of the pilot. We will provide an auditable export of region-tagged logs after the run.
- Network: we will send the VPC peering steps and the list of IPs by EOD — we can also offer marketplace/VPC option if your security prefers that route.

Schedule & asks
- Perf window confirmed: Tue 2027-06-22 09:00-11:00 PT. We will provision nodes 24 hours prior and run a lightweight health check at 08:30 PT.
- Please confirm the 5 sample conversations and the anonymized EU CID are cleared for use in the perf run (no PII).
- Please confirm if you want us to run the APAC traffic through US by default or hold APAC traffic to a higher latency option. We recommend routing APAC to US for now and revisiting once APAC volume warrants local presence.

Deliverables after the run
- Quant latency matrix (per-region p50/p95/p99), throughput graphs, and a short findings note with recommended tuning and cost estimate for 3-month pilot.

Next immediate steps: once you confirm the sample payloads and VPC peering preference, Rishi will share the peering checklist and Dylan will send the perf harness.

Thanks — looking forward to the test.

Laura Bennett | Senior Product Manager, Field Solutions | Redwood Inference
